custom_commands:
cat > /usr/local/bin/arch-project-bootstrap.sh << 'BOOTSTRAP_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/arch-project-bootstrap.log) 2>&1
echo "[arch-project] first-boot bootstrap starting"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -fsS --max-time 5 https://github.com >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 5
done
REPO_URL="https://github.com/fenn0046/archinstaller.git"
DEST=/home/archuser/arch-project
if [ -d "$DEST/.git" ]; then
  sudo -u archuser git -C "$DEST" pull
else
  sudo -u archuser git clone "$REPO_URL" "$DEST"
fi
cd "$DEST"
ansible-playbook site.yml
systemctl disable arch-project-bootstrap.service
echo "[arch-project] bootstrap complete"
BOOTSTRAP_EOF
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/arch-project-bootstrap.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/arch-project-bootstrap.service << 'UNIT_EOF'
[Unit]
Description=arch-project first-boot bootstrap
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/arch-project/provisioned

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/arch-project-bootstrap.sh
RemainAfterExit=yes
StandardOutput=journal+console
StandardError=journal+console

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT_EOF
systemctl enable arch-project-bootstrap.service
# VMware's EFI firmware does not auto-scan the UEFI fallback path
# (\EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI) on a FIXED disk - it only boots what's
# registered in NVRAM. bootloader_config.removable=true guarantees the
# fallback file exists (which most other firmware boots happily), but it
# makes grub-install skip efibootmgr entirely, so on VMware you end up
# with a perfectly valid, completely unbootable disk. Verified directly:
# correct GPT ESP GUID, valid PE32+ BOOTX64.EFI, clean FAT32 - and the
# firmware still reported 'No compatible bootloader found'.
# So register the entry explicitly here. Non-fatal: if NVRAM writes fail
# (which is what started this whole detour), the fallback file is still
# there and other firmware still boots fine.
ESP_DEV=$(findmnt -no SOURCE /boot || true)
if [ -n "$ESP_DEV" ]; then
  ESP_NAME=$(basename "$ESP_DEV")
  ESP_DISK=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ESP_DEV" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  ESP_PART=$(cat "/sys/class/block/$ESP_NAME/partition" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [ -n "$ESP_DISK" ]; then
    efibootmgr --create --disk "/dev/$ESP_DISK" --part "$ESP_PART" --loader '\EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI' --label 'Arch Linux' || echo '[arch-project] WARNING: efibootmgr failed; relying on the UEFI fallback path instead.' >&2
  fi
fi
